discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / ultracold quantum gases
motivation: Zoller and co-workers proposed in 1998 that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable parameters. In 2002 Greiner and Bloch observed the quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator, turning Bose-Einstein condensates from objects of study into programmable simulators of condensed-matter Hamiltonians. Greiner later introduced the quantum gas microscope, imaging and controlling strongly correlated matter atom by atom, while Bloch's group established many-body localization, antiferromagnetic correlations and topological band measurements. Zoller's theoretical program, including lattice gauge theories and Rydberg-based schemes, laid the foundations of analog quantum simulation as a field. Together these works created a new experimental paradigm, adopted by laboratories worldwide including in developing countries, linking atomic physics to condensed matter, high-energy theory and quantum information. It is the natural sequel to the Nobel-recognized achievements of laser cooling and Bose-Einstein condensation.
